newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba looking closely at minimum reserves - Welteke.
newsitem.headline: Buba looking closely at minimum reserves - Welteke.

text.p: The Bundesbank is analysing the possibility of paring back reserve requirements to help foster repo business but a decision must be weighed carefully, Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday.

Welteke, speaking to a group of international bankers, said that a special committee at the Bundesbank was currently studying demands, mostly from German banks, to reduce the minimum reserve requirements.

"A key element will be whether and in what way it can be assured that longer dated loans, on which reserves must be held, will not be transformed into repo business," Welteke said according to the text of a speech.

Banks have called on the Bundesbank to pare back its reserve requirements on time, sight and savings deposits, arguing that the Bundesbank's restrictions prevent repo business from gaining ground in Germany.
This in turn weakens Germany's position as a financial centre.
The reserve level is two percent of sight and term deposits and 1.5 percent of savings deposits.

Even though the Bundesbank has pared back its reserve requirements in recent years, Germany still lacks a functioning securities repurchase market as banks prefer to give such business to foreign units to avoid holding reserves.

Economists regret the absence of a functioning domestic repo market, saying this market gap could be eliminated if the Bundesbank were to eliminate requirements that banks hold reserves on these borrowed funds.
